pr_body:
Currently, the AsyncTaskCache for remote execution uses the digest as a key to determine whether or not a task has already been run. Normally this works if there is only a single cache in use. However, when using a disk cache and a remote cache, some calls try to upload files using only a single cache through one code path and another cache through another code path.

This is problematic if only disk caching is used through one code path, when remote caching is enabled though another code path (ie, uploading BES referenced artifacts), the files are not uploaded to the remote cache since the digest is the same. This change uses a String of the digest and the cache type as the key rather than just the digest to allow for uploading to both caches.

The download path is not affected by this bug, so we don't need to make any changes there.

Also, update the combined cache test to reflect what should happen:
when remote_build_event_upload=all, *all* files referenced in the BES
stream are uploaded, including build artifacts (this test now functions as intended based on documentation due to this change).


Fixes #20962, #20296
pr_title: Account for cache type for uploads in AsyncTaskCache

So, the `ensureInputsPresent_multipleConsumers_interruptedOneDuringUploadBlobs_keepInProgressUploadTasks` can fail in one of two places (lines 493-497 in RemoteCacheTest.java):

```
      if (file.equals(foo)) {
        assertThat(future.isCancelled()).isTrue();  // (1)
      } else {
        assertThat(future.isCancelled()).isFalse(); // (2)
      }
```

I believe failures in (1) are always flaky (cancellation hasn't yet propagated to the future by the time the assertion is made). While testing, I suggest adding a `Thread.sleep(1000)` before this line, which in my experience makes the flake go away. (We need to figure out a proper fix, but this PR isn't the right place for it.)

Failures in (2), on the other hand, are deterministic. I think you're theory is correct and an AsyncTaskCache is required to implement cancellation correctly. But I really don't want to delete these tests, because cancellation is important to get right.

WDYT about also adding an AsyncTaskCache to InMemoryCacheClient (assuming that does indeed fix the test failures)? This way, we still verify that the integration between RemoteExecutionCache and (a fake implementation of a) RemoteCacheClient works properly. We're going to have to rethink how to extend the tests to cover the real implementations, but again, I think it's fair to leave it for later.

We need a mock because this test needs to simulate the case where a thread is interrupted before the future returned by `uploadFile` completes. Calling the real implementation won't work because it would return a future that eventually completes, so it's impossible to write the test in a non-racy way. (I could have realized this earlier and save you the trouble, sorry.)

I think the options are to either use a completely fake implementation (in which case we aren't testing anything except the fake, and might as well delete the test), or to use one of the real implementations, but add a way to prevent the future from completing for test purposes, while still keeping the AsyncTaskCache logic in place. Or, even better: introduce an abstract class containing only the AsyncTaskCache logic, which GrpcRemoteCacheClient and DiskCacheClient inherit from; then the test can provide its own subclass that returns futures in the right state.

I cannot accept a change that just deletes the affected tests because, quite frankly, I won't otherwise be able to convince myself that we haven't introduced a regression. But I would completely understand if you don't have the time or motivation to keep working on this; it won't be forgotten and we will eventually get round to it, but it might take a while for us to find the time to do so.

The real issue with the test is that previously, the test methods would not even be called because they were cached at a higher level and this fake implementation is wrong now. What these series of tests are verifying are that:
 - If thread A and thread B are trying to upload the files, and thread B is canceled, only the futures unique to thread B should be canceled.

I think this is the source of the flakiness, right now, depending on which call happens last, that future gets put into the map and that future is checked. If that future is thread A, then the test passes because it is canceled, but if it is thread B, then it is not canceled.
